profile.campus: Aligned Northern Virginia campus (Ashburn/Data Center Alley)

source.basis: Operator location page, structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: Aligned IAD-02 sits at 21821 Uunet Drive in Ashburn, Virginia, the second building on Aligned Data Centers Northern Virginia campus, adjacent to the earlier IAD-01 facility. Per the operator own press materials, construction began in mid-2020 with a two-story, 513,000 square foot building designed to be expandable to 120 megawatts of critical capacity, with an initial phase targeting roughly 40 megawatts by the end of 2020 and topping out reported in December 2020. Together, IAD-01 and IAD-02 make up a campus that Aligned press materials describe as planned for roughly 180 megawatts total. The general contractor on the project was HITT, per trade coverage of the topping-out. Aligned, formerly Aligned Energy, describes its overall footprint today as more than fifty campuses and roughly five gigawatts of contracted and available capacity across the Americas, with Latin American operations under the ODATA brand. Ownership has changed hands several times: Macquarie Infrastructure Partners invested in April 2018 alongside BlueMountain Capital Management, Mubadala Investment Company took a minority stake in August 2023 with Macquarie Asset Management remaining majority partner, CenterSquare Investment Management invested in April 2024, and Macquarie led a capital raise exceeding 12 billion dollars in January 2025. In October 2025 a consortium named AI Infrastructure Partnership, combining BlackRock Global Infrastructure Partners and MGX, agreed to acquire all of Aligned equity from Macquarie and its co-investors in a transaction valued near 40 billion dollars, with Aligned own materials pointing to a close around July 2026, a date this research could not independently confirm via a dedicated press release. No specific tenant is disclosed for IAD-02 in any source reviewed. Aligned own facility naming pattern, IAD for Washington Dulles airport code plus a sequence number, is consistent across its Northern Virginia buildings and mirrors the airport-code convention used broadly across the colocation industry for market shorthand.
profile.research_note: 513,000 sqft and expandable-to-120MW design sourced to Aligned own June 2020 PR and Dec 2020 topping-out coverage. Initial 40MW phase target and 180MW campus-wide plan noted in reading text rather than fact-box to avoid conflating phase figures with final building capacity. Ownership/acquisition context same as other Aligned rows this operator.

reading.body:
Aligned IAD-02 is a 513,000 square foot building in Ashburn, Virginia with 120 megawatts of planned IT capacity, making it part of a two-building Northern Virginia campus that the operator describes as planned for roughly 180 megawatts total. The facility is designed to Tier III standards, which qualifies it for continuous operation with redundant cooling and power systems. At typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, 120 megawatts of IT load would supply roughly 3,000 racks, though this is an assumption about how the operator will use the space and not a published figure.

Virginia publishes capacity figures for 23 data center facilities. IAD-02 ranks 24th by stated capacity, just outside the top published sites in the state. The state's 326 mapped facilities represent only a subset of actual capacity, since most publish no figures. The state's total published capacity stands at 1,375.4 megawatts across the sites that disclose numbers, with IAD-02 accounting for 8.7 percent of that total.

The facility sits in Data Center Alley, Ashburn's concentration of hyperscale infrastructure near Washington Dulles airport, and began construction in mid-2020 with an initial phase targeting roughly 40 megawatts by end of year. No specific tenant is published for the building. The operator describes a footprint today of more than fifty campuses and roughly five gigawatts of capacity across the Americas, placing this single facility within a much larger footprint but not uniquely large within it.
